correctness.rationale: With t nonempty rows, every column is a word and exactly m of the m^t words are constant. Allocate distinct nonconstant words to the r nonconstant classes, and distinct constant words to the at most m constant classes. At the least feasible t, duplicate rows are impossible: deleting a duplicate position leaves both forms of distinction intact and contradicts minimality. If r=0, one row suffices. For extraction include all m constant functions: the first row has m classes and each additional selected row strictly refines the restrictions of the m+r distinct functions until all are separated, in at most r more rows. In the binary staircase, deleting an endpoint makes a column constant and deleting an interior row identifies adjacent columns; these failures persist under further restrictions. This works inside any m≥2. For the specified logic, match the distinct constant values by a permutation of M and extend the pair of teams by witnessing a weak quantifier with corresponding single values. The profile is preserved on extended variable lists, so induction on atoms, weak connectives and weak quantifiers proves the same invariance as the cited lemma. Weak negation of equality is not a pointwise disequality atom. The conjunction of negated constancy and pairwise negated equality forces r=k, proving sharpness of the uniform nonempty witness cutoff. The finite checker was inspected, not executed or used as a general proof.
